sub_theme: The Very Hungry Caterpillar / Life Cycles

lessons.title: Story Time: 'The Very Hungry Caterpillar' by Eric Carle
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to recall the foods the caterpillar ate in order.
lessons.main_activity: Read the story, encouraging children to join in and recall the sequence of foods eaten each day.
key_questions: What did the caterpillar eat on Monday?
What happened after he ate so much?

differentiation.extension: Recall the full week's foods in order

lessons.assessment_notes: Note comprehension and sequencing recall — evidence for LIT.1.
lessons.home_link: Retell the story to someone at home.

lessons.title: The Butterfly Life Cycle
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to name the four stages of a butterfly's life cycle.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the chick life cycle from Week 24.
lessons.main_activity: Introduce the four stages of a butterfly life cycle (egg, caterpillar, chrysalis, butterfly) using picture sequence cards.

differentiation.extension: Sequence and explain all 4 stages independently

lessons.assessment_notes: Note understanding of a second life cycle example — evidence for UTW.3.
lessons.plenary: Recap the four life cycle stages.
lessons.home_link: Look for a caterpillar or butterfly together if possible.

lessons.title: Counting the Caterpillar's Food
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to count the quantities of food eaten in the story.
lessons.main_activity: Children count out the quantities of food the caterpillar ate each day (1 apple, 2 pears, 3 plums...) using counters, checking accuracy.
key_questions: How many pears did he eat?
Can you count them again to check?

differentiation.extension: Count up to 5 and add totals across days

lessons.assessment_notes: Record counting accuracy in a story context — evidence for MATHS.1.
lessons.plenary: Class total food count from the story.

lessons.title: Writing Days of the Week
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to attempt to write or recognise the days of the week from the story.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the days of the week using the story's structure.
lessons.main_activity: Children practise recognising/attempting to write the days of the week, linking each to what the caterpillar ate.
resources_needed: Days of the week cards, paper, pencils
key_questions: What did the caterpillar eat that day?

differentiation.extension: Attempt to write day names independently

lessons.assessment_notes: Note recognition of days of the week — evidence for LIT.3/UTW.1.
lessons.plenary: Recap the days of the week in order.
lessons.home_link: Practise the days of the week together at home.

lessons.title: Comparing Chick and Butterfly Life Cycles
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to identify a similarity and a difference between two life cycles.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap both life cycles learned (chick and butterfly).
lessons.main_activity: Children compare the chick and butterfly life cycles side by side, noting similarities (both start as eggs) and differences (number of stages).
key_questions: What is similar about these life cycles?

differentiation.support: Point to one similarity with support

lessons.assessment_notes: Note comparative scientific reasoning — evidence for UTW.3.
lessons.plenary: Class recap of similarities and differences found.
lessons.home_link: Compare two animal life cycles you know about at home.

lessons.title: Ordering the Butterfly Life Cycle with Ordinal Numbers
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to order the life cycle stages using ordinal numbers.
lessons.main_activity: Children order butterfly life cycle picture cards using ordinal number labels (first: egg, second: caterpillar...).
resources_needed: Life cycle sequencing cards, ordinal number labels

differentiation.extension: Use ordinal language independently for all 4 stages

lessons.assessment_notes: Note ordinal number and sequencing understanding — evidence for MATHS.1/UTW.3.
lessons.plenary: Class recap of the life cycle order using ordinal numbers.
lessons.home_link: Practise ordinal numbers with a sequence at home.

lessons.title: Retelling 'The Very Hungry Caterpillar'
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to retell the whole story using props and sequencing.
lessons.main_activity: In small groups, children retell the full story using food props and a caterpillar puppet.

differentiation.support: Retell with adult prompting at each stage

lessons.assessment_notes: Note full narrative retelling ability — evidence for LIT.1/CL.2.
lessons.plenary: One group performs their retelling to the class.
lessons.home_link: Retell the whole story to your family.

lessons.title: Observing a Real Caterpillar (If Available) or Video
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to make an observation about a real or filmed caterpillar.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the life cycle learned this week.
lessons.main_activity: (If class has caterpillars) observe and discuss; otherwise watch a short age-appropriate video of a caterpillar becoming a butterfly and discuss observations.

differentiation.support: Watch and describe with adult prompts
differentiation.extension: Describe the process in detail independently

lessons.assessment_notes: Note observational and scientific language — evidence for UTW.3.
lessons.home_link: Watch a nature video about caterpillars/butterflies together if possible.

lessons.title: Symmetry in Butterfly Wings
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to create a symmetrical pattern on butterfly wings.
lessons.main_activity: Children paint one half of a butterfly wing shape, fold it, and press to create a symmetrical print (blow-painting or paper-fold technique).
key_questions: Is your pattern the same on both sides?
How did folding help create symmetry?

differentiation.extension: Predict what the symmetrical result will look like before unfolding

lessons.assessment_notes: Note symmetry understanding and prediction — evidence for MATHS.2/EAD.1.
lessons.home_link: Try a fold-and-paint symmetry activity at home.

lessons.title: Writing About the Caterpillar's Feelings
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to attempt to write how the caterpillar felt at different points.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap how the caterpillar felt throughout the story.
lessons.main_activity: Children draw the caterpillar at different story points and attempt to write a feeling word (hungry, full) using known phonics sounds.
key_questions: How did the caterpillar feel here?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note writing progress and emotional vocabulary — evidence for LIT.3/PSED.1.
lessons.plenary: Share feeling word pictures with a partner.
lessons.home_link: Talk about feeling hungry and full with family.

lessons.title: Healthy vs Unhealthy Food Recap (Story Link)
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to identify which foods in the story were healthy vs treats.
lessons.main_activity: Sort the foods the caterpillar ate into 'healthy' and 'treat' categories, discussing why he felt poorly after eating too many treats.
resources_needed: Food picture cards from the story
key_questions: Why did the caterpillar feel poorly?

differentiation.extension: Explain the balance needed between healthy food and treats

lessons.assessment_notes: Note application of prior healthy-eating learning to a new context — evidence for UTW.3.
lessons.plenary: Recap the importance of balanced eating.
lessons.home_link: Talk about balancing healthy food and treats at home.

lessons.title: Number Bonds Recap: Caterpillar Theme
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to recall number bonds to 10 using a caterpillar-themed activity.
lessons.main_activity: Using a caterpillar made of 10 linking segments, children split it into two groups to explore number bonds to 10.
key_questions: What are all the ways to make 10?
Can you recall this without counting?
lessons.assessment_notes: Assess number bond to 10 fluency — evidence for MATHS.1.
lessons.plenary: Class recap of all bonds to 10.
lessons.home_link: Practise number bonds to 10 with any small objects at home.

lessons.title: Phonics: Reading Caterpillar Story Words
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to blend and read simple story-themed words.
lessons.main_activity: Phonics stations reading story-themed word cards and simple sentences (e.g. 'the bug ate a leaf').

differentiation.support: Read simple CVC words with support

lessons.assessment_notes: Note phonics application to themed vocabulary — evidence for LIT.2.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate reading progress with a themed reading game.
lessons.home_link: Practise reading story words over the weekend.

lessons.title: Life Cycles Recap Display
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to summarise key facts about the butterfly life cycle and compare it to the chick life cycle.
lessons.main_activity: Contribute to a class 'Life Cycles' display summarising the butterfly life cycle alongside the chick life cycle from Week 24.
resources_needed: Large display paper, week's work, Week 24 materials
key_questions: What have we learned about life cycles?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note synthesis and comparison across two life cycle topics — evidence for UTW.3.
lessons.home_link: Share what you learned about life cycles with your family.

lessons.title: Maths Review: Counting, Ordinals, Symmetry
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to apply counting, ordinal numbers, and symmetry skills learned this week.
lessons.main_activity: Rotate through 3 stations: counting caterpillar food, ordinal life cycle sequencing, symmetry butterfly recap.
lessons.plenary: Class recap game combining all three skills.
lessons.home_link: Continue practising counting and symmetry over the weekend.
